answer: An employer of record files a quarterly return naming one worker, one tax number; the ledger reads that filing as the attestation. Payroll records behave like quartz, accreting one filing at a time; none back-fills four quarters overnight. The tax number is the cipher each claim decodes against, so two addresses that share one collapse to a vote and forfeit the epoch. A thousand clones need a thousand registrations, each with an unemployment deposit and a bookkeeper under perjury: $800,000 a year before payout. An honest hire slides through like velvet; the thousandth hits a bricked door.
